claims.text: Team Topologies is a canonical book on organising software teams; it names four team types (stream-aligned, platform, enabling, complicated-subsystem) so each team's purpose and relation to other teams are explicit.
claims.source_hint: Team Topologies (book), chapter on the four fundamental team topologies; no author or year in the lesson

claims.text: Definitions as Team Topologies gives them: stream-aligned team owns one flow of change for a part of the business, idea to production; platform team provides internal services lowering stream-aligned teams' cognitive load.
claims.source_hint: Team Topologies (book), sections on stream-aligned and platform teams

claims.text: Per Team Topologies: the other three types exist to reduce stream-aligned teams' cognitive load; an enabling team helps a team gain a skill for a limited time, takes no work from it, then steps back; a complicated-subsystem team owns a part needing rare knowledge.
claims.source_hint: Team Topologies (book), sections on enabling and complicated-subsystem teams and on cognitive load

claims.text: ADR 0025 option B splits by layer (front end DonHang.App; back end api, Notifications, Payments; operations cluster, CI, on-call); almost every change a shop would notice passes all three: screen, endpoint, deploy and alert.

Option C: two stream-aligned teams — Đặt hàng (Ordering, Payments, Notifications, lib/features/ordering) and Cửa hàng (Catalog, opening new shops, lib/features/catalog and lib/features/auth) — plus a platform team.

The platform team gets OpenTofu, Argo CD and the config repo, Gateway, Sealed Secrets, Prometheus, admission policy, templates/dotnet-service and the golden path — most of the capabilities in platform-capabilities.md, but not the CI jobs listed there — plus running PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ and Keycloak.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0025-... @ stage-4 lines 42-44; docs/team/platform-capabilities.md @ stage-4 table 'Năng lực đang có'

claims.text: ADR 0025 lines 46-49: each stream-aligned team makes a change from idea to production without waiting; the platform team keeps the shared part so the others need not know the cluster to the bottom; price: drawing lines and clear owners for parts between teams.

ADR 0025 chooses C; team lines follow module/service lines; only the module contract ICatalog sits between the stream-aligned teams; it rejects A (one bigger team: more pairs, no lower load per person) and B (almost every visible change needs all three teams, waits at two handoffs).

Shared parts get owners: lib/design/, lib/shared/ and the api's Program.cs held by Đặt hàng (Cửa hàng sends pull requests); Keycloak run by the platform team; lib/features/auth belongs to Cửa hàng. Lines 68-70: team formation order; 71-73: on-call split by team.
No complicated-subsystem team yet: invoice signing in the provider's HSM (ADR 0023) has no code that runs against that HSM yet, so it is the first candidate once built.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0025-... @ stage-4 lines 74-75; docs/team/team-structure.md @ stage-4 lines 57-58; docs/adr/0023-... @ stage-4 'Quyết định'

claims.text: Neither option B nor option C in ADR 0025 includes an enabling team (the plan table in team-structure.md likewise lists no enabling team).
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0025-... @ stage-4 lines 32-44; docs/team/team-structure.md @ stage-4 lines 44-48

claims.text: Among ADR 0025's conditions to reopen: once the invoice signing of ADR 0023 is built, review whether a complicated-subsystem team is needed.

Catalog is a module inside the api (ADR line 21). Product endpoint ProductsController (not named in ADR 0025) reads via ICatalog, so a new product field changes what it returns; Ordering's CatalogProductPrices (DonHang.Infrastructure) reads prices via ICatalog too.
Team types name the kind of job a team does for the flow of change, not a technical layer; a layer team owns a slice of every change, so each change crosses teams.

Trade-offs: layer split rarely fits product work; stream-aligned plus platform fits when module/service lines exist; a team per specialism fits only rare knowledge in a part large enough to own; an enabling team fits when several teams lack the same skill at once.

Choices not recorded in Đơn Hàng's files (hedged): with built HSM signing known by one person, weigh rarity and size before a new team; a security team reviewing every change becomes a handoff; a missing skill fits limited-time help; signing might fit a dedicated team only if a review finds it rare.

Possible symptoms (hedged): a small feature becomes cards on three teams' boards and ships at the slowest pace; the same team still asked for the same task months later; a specialist team's queue becomes the step every change waits on.
